pairs.description: Licorice-induced hypokalemia dramatically increases myocardial sensitivity to digoxin, precipitating life-threatening cardiac dysrhythmias.
pairs.mechanism: Glycyrrhizin inhibits 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, producing pseudoaldosteronism and severe potassium depletion.

pairs.description: Combining licorice root with loop diuretics like furosemide accelerates renal potassium wasting, causing profound hypokalemia.
pairs.mechanism: Additive kaliuretic actions from loop diuretic inhibition of Na-K-2Cl symporters and mineralocorticoid excess.

pairs.description: Licorice root may induce CYP2C9 enzymes and alter warfarin clearance, potentially decreasing anticoagulant efficacy and INR levels.
pairs.mechanism: Mild induction of hepatic CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 metabolic pathways by triterpenoid constituents.

pairs.description: Licorice components antagonize the aldosterone-receptor blocking action of spironolactone, abolishing its diuretic and antihypertensive effects.
pairs.mechanism: Cortisol-mediated activation of renal mineralocorticoid receptors overpowering competitive spironolactone antagonism.
